'''Mohamed Diawara''' (born 29 April 2005)<ref name=":0">{{cite web |url=https://parisbasketball.paris/joueur/mohamed-diawara/# |title=Mohamed Diawara |work=Paris Basketball |access-date=6 October 2022}}</ref> is a French professional [[basketball]] player for the [[New York Knicks]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He previously played for [[Cholet Basket]] of the [[LNB Élite]]. Standing at {{height|ft=6|in=9}}, he plays in the [[power forward]] position. In his rookie season, his team won the [[2026 NBA Finals]].

==Professional career==
===Paris Basketball===
Diawara began his basketball career with the Parisian club La Domremy Basket 13 and later played for the youth team of Saint Charles Basket in Charenton-le-Pont.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.saintcharlesbasket.fr/articles/56649-decouvrez-mohamed-diawara |title=Découvrez Mohamed Diawara |work=Saint Charles Basket |date=2020 |access-date=6 October 2022}}</ref> In the 2020–21 season, he was trained at the French academy [[INSEP]]<ref name=":0" /> and moved to [[Paris Basketball]] in the summer of 2021,<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{cite web |url=https://basket-ballworld.fr/paris-basketball-ambitions/ |title=Elite : Le Paris Basketball affiche ses ambitions |work=basket-ballworld.fr |date=25 September 2021 |access-date=6 October 2022}}</ref> for which he made his first appearances in the French first division in the following 2021–22 season.<ref name=":0" /> In the summer of 2022, he was named the best player at the [[Basketball Without Borders]] talent scouting event organized by the world governing body [[FIBA]] and the [[National Basketball Association|NBA]] in [[Milan]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bebasket.fr/mohamed-diawara-et-leila-lacan-deux-francais-mvp-du-basketball-without-borders-europe/ |title=Mohamed Diawara et Leila Lacan : deux Français MVP du Basketball Without Borders Europe |work=BeBasket |date=5 June 2022 |access-date=6 October 2022}}</ref>

===Poitiers Basket and Cholet Basket===
In December 2023, Diawara was loaned to second-division club [[Poitiers Basket 86]],<ref>{{cite web |url=https://parisbasketball.com/2023/12/diawara-prete-a-poitiers-jusqua-la-fin-de-saison/ |title=Diawara prêté à Poitiers jusqu'à la fin de saison |work=Paris Basketball |date=20 December 2023 |language=fr |access-date=23 April 2024}}</ref> after receiving little playing time in Paris during the previous 2023–24 season. He was signed by first-division club [[Cholet Basket]] during the 2024 summer break.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bebasket.fr/avec-cholet-mohamed-diawara-va-vouloir-montrer-quil-a-les-epaules-pour-la-nba |title=Avec Cholet, Mohamed Diawara va vouloir montrer qu'il a les épaules pour la NBA |work=Bebasket.fr |date=13 September 2024 |language=fr |access-date=13 September 2024}}</ref>

===New York Knicks===
On 26 June 2025, Diawara was drafted by the [[Los Angeles Clippers]] with the 51st overall pick of the second round of the [[2025 NBA draft]], who traded his rights to the [[New York Knicks]] for the rights to [[Kobe Sanders]].<ref>{{cite web |language=fr |first=Giovanni |last=Marriette |title=Draft 2025 : le Français Mohamed Diawara drafté en 51 par les Knicks ! |url=https://trashtalk.co/2025/06/27/nba-draft-2025-le-francais-mohamed-diawara-drafte-en-51-par-les-new-york-knicks/ |website=TrashTalk |date=2025-06-27 |access-date=2025-06-27}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.lequipe.fr/Basket/Actualites/Noah-penda-maxime-raynaud-et-mohamed-diawara-selectionnes-au-2e-tour-de-la-draft-nba/1573380|title=Noah Penda, Maxime Raynaud et Mohamed Diawara sélectionnés au 2e tour de la draft NBA|date=27 June 2025|publisher=L'Équipe}}</ref>

On 29 December 2025, against the [[New Orleans Pelicans]], Diawara recorded a career-high 18 points in 18 minutes, making all 4 of his three-point shots.<ref>{{cite web |language=en |first=Kris |last=Pursiainen |title=The Knicks' best rookie just sent a message Mike Brown can't afford to ignore |url=https://dailyknicks.com/knicks-rookie-message-mike-brown-cant-afford-to-ignore/ |website=DailyKnicks.com |date=2025-12-29 |access-date=2025-12-30}}</ref>

On 1 March 2026, against the [[San Antonio Spurs]], Diawara scored 14 points in just 15 minutes off the bench, on 5-14 (35.7%) shooting, also securing 4 rebounds. The Knicks beat the Spurs 114–89, ending the Spurs' eleven-game winning streak, despite strong play from Spurs star and fellow Frenchman Victor Wembanyama.<ref>{{cite web |language=en |first=Jared |last=Schwartz |title=Mohamed Diawara reclaims his spot in pecking order during Knicks' win: 'Doesn't bat an eye'
 |url=https://nypost.com/2026/03/01/sports/mohamed-diawara-reclaims-his-spot-in-pecking-order-during-knicks-win/ |website=NYPost.com |date=2026-03-02 |access-date=2026-03-02}}</ref>

On 4 March 2026, against the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]], Diawara scored 9 points in just 13 minutes off the bench, making 3-4 of his three-point shots. Despite his hot shooting, he played only 3 minutes in the second half, and the Knicks lost to the Thunder 103–100.

On 13 June 2026, Diawara and the Knicks won the [[2026 NBA Finals]], beating the [[San Antonio Spurs]] 4–1.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://clutchpoints.com/nba/new-york-knicks/knicks-news-first-championship-53-years-nba-finals-spurs|title=Knicks win first championship in 53 years after NBA Finals Game 5 triumph vs. Spurs|website=[[ClutchPoints]]|last=Siegel|first=Brett|date=June 13, 2026|access-date=June 13, 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/news/live-updates-2026-nba-finals-game-5-knicks-seek-first-title-since-1973|title=Recap: The Knicks win the 2026 NBA championship|website=[[NBA.com]]|last=Lambert|first=Ben|date=June 13, 2026|access-date=June 13, 2026}}</ref>

On June 22, 2026, Diawara re-signed with the Knicks on a four-year, $10 million contract.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://clutchpoints.com/nba/new-york-knicks/knicks-news-ny-signs-restricted-free-agent-mohamed-diawara-multi-year-contract-worth-over-10-million|title=Knicks sign restricted free agent to multi-year contract worth over $10 million |work=[[ClutchPoints]] |date=22 June 2026 |language= |access-date=13 September 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=NEW YORK KNICKS RE-SIGN MOHAMED DIAWARA|url=https://www.nba.com/knicks/news/new-york-knicks-re-sign-mohamed-diawara|website=NBA.com|date=July 6, 2026|access-date=July 13, 2026}}</ref>

==National team career==
Diawara played for the [[France men's national under-17 basketball team|France under-17 basketball team]] at the [[2022 FIBA Under-17 Basketball World Cup]], in which his team won the bronze medal.<ref>{{cite web |date=10 July 2022 |title=Les Bleuets décrochent le bronze à la Coupe du monde U17 contre la Lituanie |url=https://www.lequipe.fr/Basket/Actualites/Les-bleuets-decrochent-le-bronze-a-la-coupe-du-monde-u17-contre-la-lituanie/1342989 |access-date=23 February 2023 |work=[[L'Équipe]] |language=fr}}</ref>
